title: range connector with multiple attributes
body:
Looking at the [beta docs on custom connectors](https://github.com/algolia/react-instantsearch/blob/master/docgen/src/guide/Custom_connectors.md) and since `connectRange` doesn't serve my use case I thought I would post it here before taking a stab at the custom connector. 

A sample record looks like
```js
{
  objectID: "asdfasdf",
  minValue: 2,
  maxValue: 5
  ...
}
```
I would like to use a range connector to find records that fall within a specific range. If the user enters ranges like `1 to 3` or `2 to 3` or `4 to 7` for value then I'd like this record to show. Seems like [this is possible](https://www.algolia.com/doc/guides/search/filtering-faceting/#filter-by-numerical-value) by using multiple numeric refinements but the default `connectRange` component only takes a single `attributeName`. Is there another way to go about this without creating a custom component?

comments.body:
Hi @mvanlonden,

If I understand correctly you're trying to recreate the [`<RangeInput/>`](https://community.algolia.com/react-instantsearch/widgets/RangeInput.html) but having the min and the max being inside two different attributes? 

May I ask what's your business use case behind this?

Sure. I'm creating a filterable list of house designs which includes filtering by attributes like square footage, price, number of bedrooms and number of bathrooms. A design might have multiple variants like "with garage" or "with double master suite" which could specify different values for any of the attributes. A record in algolia represents the base model and all of its variants. So if the base model has 3 bedrooms and one of its variants, "with double master suite", adds an additional bedroom then that record can have 3-4 bedrooms.

@mvanlonden: in that case, isn't it possible to use multiple `connectRange`? 

One for the main attributes, and one for its variants. 
Then each connected component should only display one input and set the min === max. 

Will this work?

I'm not sure I understand. You mean nesting the hoc? Since a base model can
have multiple variants there is a range of values for an attribute in the
data model. The base model might have 3 bedrooms and it might have 4
variants one with 4 bedrooms, one with 5, another with 4, and one with 6.
So then in the algolia record there​ is a minBedrooms attribute of 3 and a
maxBedrooms attribute of 6. Does your solution cover this use case or does
it only work for a single variant?

just returning to this @mthuret / @mvanlonden - I have a business use case here whereby we have a min and max occupancy of a trip.. e.g. a trip can take between 4 and 10 people. I would like to have a simple input where I only show trips that can take 5 people.

my doc would look something like this:
````

   minPax: 4,
````

@samouss you might also be interested by this use case.

Hello! We came across similar requirements recently. As far as I can see, using a `min` and a `max` attribute for range inputs is still not possible out of the box, right?

We're using the `vue-instantsearch` package and have a use case where one product requires a supplementary part of a certain size range. So for example product P needs a supplementary part with a size between 6.5 and 10 meters. A potential customer (website user) is looking for a product, that fits his needs (let's say 5 to 7 meters). As both ranges overlap (product capabilities and user requirements), product P would be a fit and should be displayed.

Is it possible achieve this with `vue-instantsearch` without a complete Algolia component rewrite using a custom connector? What'd be the best approach?
The easiest method would be to use two different range widgets, one for min and one for max with the different attributes respectively
